title: Does this need combat, or am I about to ruin the vibe?
author: StefJP
selftext:
Been messing around with this planet-hopping prototype for a while. A lot of the early visual work came from experimenting with generative AI, and I’ve been building the actual journey around the results.

Flying between planets is finally starting to feel decent. The visuals and sound still need work, but the overall mood is pretty close to what I wanted.

Now I’m stuck on what the player should actually do along the way.

My first thought was ship combat, but every version I picture slowly turns it into a generic space shooter. Maybe combat should be rare. Maybe the danger should come from the planets and the environment instead. Or maybe adding combat at all is the wrong move.

What would you expect to happen next after watching this clip? Would you want fights, survival stuff, exploration, or something else?

comments.author: lesbird65
comments.body:
My Super Starship game on Steam is all about star hopping and planet hopping. You can fly from star to star (one million of them) with each star having its own unique solar system to explore. I avoided combat, it's all about exploration and discovery. If a player wants combat they can play essentially ANY of the other space games as they all seem to have that feature. Apparently space is very violent for some reason.

Super Starship was made with Unity.

I've also been experimenting with agentic AI for deep space and planet stuff. See my project here: [https://github.com/lesbird/DeepSpaceEngine](https://github.com/lesbird/DeepSpaceEngine)

It was inspired by Space Engine and runs on Mac/Windows/Linux. Essentially it is an endless procedurally generated universe, billions of galaxies with each galaxy having billions/trillions of stars, each one with a unique solar system and planets you can land on.

Does your game need combat? My answer is no.
